title: Character Schedule Blueprint
description: Declarative rebuild input/output without UUIDs, with optional display icons. Omitted collections are empty. Import rebuilds and replaces the entire project content in the current workspace, allocating new UUIDs; it does not merge or retain a separate old project. Expressions require parser and semantic validation. Execution contract: ../../docs/ENGINE_SEMANTICS.md or MCP schedule://guide/engine-semantics.
$comment: This Schema specifies structure, not the complete engine. Read ENGINE_SEMANTICS.md for selection, evaluation, priority, writes, interruption, reset and checkpoint behavior.

min.description: Optional inclusive lower bound applied on every successful write, not once at macro/day end.

max.description: Optional inclusive upper bound applied on every successful write, after integer truncation.

integer.description: Writes truncate toward zero, then clamp to optional min/max. When true, initial and any min/max must already be integers; fractional bounds are invalid definitions. Intermediate arithmetic is not truncated.

Calls use expr.name(arguments), evaluate arguments once in declaration order, then evaluate only the selected result. Environment builtins randomRange/randomItem use seeded randomness. source.description: Choose one day per event occurrence, before day execution. Random uses relative positive weights; sequential advances on occurrence even if later blocked. See ENGINE_SEMANTICS.md section 6.

cooldown_days.description: After occurrence, skip this many subsequent eligible dates. Ineligible dates do not consume cooldown; changes to this setting do not rewrite remaining cooldown.

day.description: Persistent name, unique within its object type. Blueprint references and engine contracts use this name; never a UUID.

execution.description: Per-slot behavior: overlay, interrupt_main, or interrupt_lower (strictly lower event priority plus main). Daily start/end are not blocked. See ENGINE_SEMANTICS.md sections 7-8.

priority.description: Execution order is descending; nonnegative events precede the main day, negatives follow. Ties retain declaration order. Interruption targets are defined by execution, not priority alone.
